Definitions of algorithm classes and function classes An algorithm is a mapping from real-valued functions to sequences. For algorithm A and f : Rd → R, we define A[f ] = {x(i) }i∈N to be the sequence of algorithm A acting on f , where x(i) ∈ Rd . Note here, the algorithm under our consideration works on function defined on any Euclidean space. We call it the dimension-free property of the algorithm. The definition of algorithms abstracts away from the the optimization process of a function. We consider algorithms which only make use of the first-order information of the iteration sequence.
